content:
We have a template (reaction_id 159) that is simple esterification: [CH3;D1;+0:1]-[O;H0;D2;+0:4]-[C:3]=[O;D1;H0:2]>>O-[CH3;D1;+0:1].[O;D1;H0:2]=[C:3]-[OH;D1;+0:4]

This is reverse of ester formation: It breaks ester into methanol and acid. So the retrosynthetic direction: target ester -> methanol + acid. Good.

Thus we can use this template to propose retrosynthesis: target -> methanol + acid (the acid is the corresponding carboxylic acid). So we need to get the acid SMILES: remove the methyl ester OCH3, replace with OH. The target SMILES: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. The acid would be: O=C(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)O (i.e., carboxylic acid). Let's generate that SMILES: "OC(=O)C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2". Actually need correct order: "O=C(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)O". We'll use that.

Now we need to check if methanol (SMILES "CO") and that acid are commercially available and total price <=125. We need to check buyability and price. There's no price tool, only is_buyable. Price constraint maybe not enforceable but we assume cheap.

We can check is_buyable for both.
